zotero.abstractNote: Low-field MRI scanners offer a portable and cost-effective alternative to high-field systems, but they suffer from lower signal-to-noise ratios and reduced contrast, complicating automated image segmentation. In this work, we propose a symmetric nnU-Net ResEnc architecture to segment brain regions in low-field pediatric brain MR images. Our approach leverages the structural symmetry of the brain to improve segmentation performance. We evaluate our method on the Low-Field Pediatric Brain MRI Segmentation Challenge dataset, demonstrating competitive results compared to standard nnU-Net baselines.
